Task 4 review came back: spec compliant, but **Needs fixes** on one Important finding. Your recharts investigation was sound as far as it went — the reviewer confirmed `tickFormatter`'s explicit `number` annotation is a legitimate narrowing (`TickFormatter = (value: any, index: number) => string`), and that `formatter`'s untyped parameter correctly resolves to `ValueType | undefined`. One of the three did not.

**Finding (Important): `labelFormatter`'s parameter silently infers to `any`.**

`ObservationTrendChart.tsx:68-70`:

```tsx
labelFormatter={(value) =>
  format(Number(value), "d MMM yyyy, HH:mm")
}
```

The installed recharts is **3.9.2**, not the 3.8.1 the plan assumed. It declares `labelFormatter` twice — `Tooltip.d.ts:117` has `(label: any, payload: TooltipPayload) => ReactNode`, which intersects with `DefaultTooltipContent.d.ts`'s `(label: ReactNode, payload) => ReactNode`. When TypeScript contextually types a bare arrow function against an intersection of call signatures it unions the parameter types position-wise, giving `ReactNode | any` — and `any` absorbs the union. So `value` is genuinely `any`.

The reviewer verified this empirically rather than from memory, using an `IsAny<T> = 0 extends (1 & T) ? true : false` probe against the actual installed `.d.ts`, with `string` as a negative control.

This violates the no-`any` constraint even though the word never appears in your source, and neither check you ran can see it: `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` only flags explicit annotations, and no type-aware `no-unsafe-*` rules are enabled in this repo. That's why the green run didn't catch it — not a mistake on your part, but the constraint still binds.

It matters concretely because `Number(value)` then feeds `date-fns` `format()`, and `format()` in the installed date-fns 4.4.0 throws `RangeError("Invalid time value")` on `NaN` (`node_modules/date-fns/format.js:348-350`). Worth knowing: `seriesForCode` in `observationPivot.ts` validates only `value` for finiteness, never `time`, so a malformed `effective_datetime` upstream would produce `NaN` for `time` with nothing left to catch it.

**The fix:** annotate explicitly as `ReactNode` (assignable to both intersection members) and narrow before formatting, rather than blind-coercing:

```tsx
labelFormatter={(label: ReactNode) =>
  typeof label === "number"
    ? format(label, "d MMM yyyy, HH:mm")
    : String(label ?? "")
}
```

Import `ReactNode` as a type-only import from `react`. Adapt the exact shape if something about it doesn't fit — the requirement is a real compile-time contract on that parameter and no unguarded `Number()` into `format()`, not this literal snippet.

Please confirm in your fix report which of the three callbacks you changed and which you deliberately left alone, with the reasoning — the reviewer will check that `formatter` and `tickFormatter` were correctly left as-is.

Then re-run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint src/components/Common/Charts/observation-plot-sheet/`, and `npm run test:unit` (must still be 34/34), commit, and append the fix report to your report file with commands and output.

One separate note, no action needed: the reviewer flagged that your report described the single-point-series behaviour as "verified" when the verification section only listed `tsc`/`eslint`/`test:unit`. The claim may well be right, but please keep "verified" for things you actually exercised — I'm routing the single-point case to Task 8's visual QA instead.

Good work, and thank you for flagging the fourth call site rather than quietly matching the brief. Two follow-ups before this goes to review.

**1. Wire the fourth `DiagnosticReportResultsTable` site.**

You're right that `src/pages/Encounters/tabs/diagnostic-reports.tsx` is a real fourth render site my plan never mentioned — I only had View, Print and Review. My ruling: wire it. It already has `patientId` and `encounterId` in scope, and leaving it inert would make the same table clickable on one route and dead on another, which reads as a bug rather than a deliberate boundary. Pass the two props exactly as you did in `DiagnosticReportView.tsx`. Print and Review stay untouched.

**2. Guard unparseable timestamps in `observationPivot.ts` — this is a crash, not a nicety.**

The Task 4 re-review noted in passing that `seriesForCode` validates `value` for finiteness but never `time`. I traced how far that actually reaches, and it's worse than it was scoped:

- `pivotObservations` sets `column.time = new Date(key).getTime()`. A malformed `effective_datetime` makes that `NaN`.
- `labelColumns` then calls `format(column.time, "yyyy-MM-dd")`.
- I confirmed empirically that date-fns v4 `format(NaN, …)` throws `RangeError: Invalid time value`.

So a **single** malformed `effective_datetime` anywhere in the response crashes the entire sheet render — not just a tooltip. Please fix it in `src/components/Common/Charts/observation-plot-sheet/observationPivot.ts`:

- In `pivotObservations`, skip any observation whose `effective_datetime` does not parse to a finite time, the same way unmatched `main_code` readings are already skipped. A reading we cannot place on a timeline has no column to go in.
- In `seriesForCode`, apply the same guard to `time` that already exists for `value`.

Dropping such readings is the right trade for a clinical view: a value we cannot position in time is worse than absent, and the alternative is a blank screen.

**This module has the project's only unit test harness — add coverage.** Extend `observationPivot.test.ts` with tests pinning the new behaviour: a reading with an unparseable `effective_datetime` is excluded from `columns`, and excluded from `seriesForCode`'s points. Follow the existing `localIso(day, hour)` fixture style; note the `reading()` helper takes the datetime as a string, so passing something like `"not-a-date"` should work directly. Run them RED first if you can, so you know they actually pin the fix.

You are the final whole-branch reviewer for a completed feature branch. Every task has had its own scoped review already; this is the last gate before the branch is handed to a human for manual testing and merge.

## The Feature

An "observation plot sheet" for CARE (React 19 + TypeScript EMR frontend, a Digital Public Good building an open-source EMR). Clicking an observation anywhere in an encounter opens a sheet showing that observation's history: a trend chart plus a pivoted flowsheet table, scopeable to the current encounter or the patient's whole record.

Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-01-observation-plot-sheet-design.md`
Implementation plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-01-observation-plot-sheet.md`

Read the spec. Do not read the whole plan — it is long and the diff is what matters.

## Diff Under Review

**Merge base:** 0f8b28b0f
**Head:** c3ee1bc95
**Diff file:** `/Users/bodhishthomas/code/care_fe/.claude/worktrees/observation-plot-sheet-77acfc/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-01-observation-plot-sheet/review-0f8b28b0f..c3ee1bc95.diff`

Read the diff file — it has the 14 commits, a stat summary, and the full diff with context. Two of the changed files are the spec and plan documents themselves; skim those, focus on the code.

Your review is read-only. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state.

## Verification already performed — do not re-run

- `npm run test:unit` → 36/36 passing (34 original + 2 pinning the timestamp guard)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean
- `npx eslint` on every changed file → clean. Two warnings exist in `DiagnosticReportPrint.tsx`, which this branch does NOT touch (confirmed) — pre-existing, not this branch's.
- Prettier clean.

**A green type-check is not proof of type safety on this branch.** An earlier task shipped a parameter that silently inferred to `any` through a library type intersection, and both `tsc` and eslint passed it. If you suspect something similar, verify at the type level against the installed `.d.ts` rather than trusting the green run.

## Binding constraints from the spec

- **The `analyse` endpoint must not be used.** It calls `get_queryset()` not `filter_queryset()` server-side, so its `encounter` filter is silently ignored and it cannot honour the scope toggle. Only `observationApi.list` can.
- **`useObservationPlotData` must be the feature's only API-aware module.**
- **No reference ranges, no normal/abnormal shading, no "Abnormal only" filter.** That data is populated only for observations linked to an ObservationDefinition and is usually absent, so it was deliberately deferred.
- **Nothing may mark which readings belong to the current encounter** — the backend nulls `encounter` on every list read.
- Observations with no `main_code` must not be clickable. On a fixture database every observation has `main_code: null`, so this guard is load-bearing, not defensive noise.
- `DiagnosticReportResultsTable` renders in four places; only the two *viewing* surfaces (`DiagnosticReportView.tsx`, `Encounters/tabs/diagnostic-reports.tsx`) pass ids and become clickable. `DiagnosticReportPrint.tsx` and `DiagnosticReportReview.tsx` must stay untouched so print output stays clean.
- Code style: double quotes, 2-space indent, semicolons, `interface` for objects, no `any`, named exports, one component per file, i18n for all user-facing strings, English only in `public/locale/en.json`.

## Known deferred items — triage these, do not re-discover them

Each was reviewed and consciously deferred. Tell me which, if any, must be fixed before merge:

1. `hasRequestedPageRef` in `ObservationFlowsheetTable` has no fallback reset. It is safe only because `onLoadMore` is a raw pass-through to TanStack's `fetchNextPage`, which always transitions `isFetchingNextPage`. If a future change wraps `onLoadMore` with anything that can no-op, the ref latches `true` and silently kills scroll-pagination for the component's lifetime. A one-line comment recording that invariant was suggested.
2. `useObservationPlotData` returns no `isError`/`error`, so a failed fetch renders as "no readings" rather than surfacing failure. Matches the existing `ObservationHistoryTable`/`vitals/list` convention in this repo.
3. Single-point series: `XAxis domain={["dataMin", "dataMax"]}` gives a zero-width domain when there is exactly one point; the dot may silently fail to render.
4. `ObservationPlotSheet` uses `title || …` rather than `?? `, so an empty-string title falls through.
5. `seriesForCode`'s `seen` set is populated before the numeric guard, so a non-numeric winning amendment suppresses a superseded numeric reading at the same timestamp. Judged the correct reading of the first-wins rule, but untested.
6. No Playwright E2E test was written. The environment has no running backend, and — verified against the care backend's `data/questionnaire_fixtures.json` — all 42 fixture questions lack an observation `code`, so fixture-seeded observations have `main_code: null` and are not clickable. The human will test manually.

## What I want from you

A merge-readiness judgement, not a re-litigation of settled decisions. Specifically:

1. **Correctness bugs** the per-task reviews could not see because they only ever saw one task's diff. Cross-file integration is where these live: prop contracts across the four call sites, the pivot/hook/component data flow, state that spans components.
2. **Anything that breaks an existing surface.** This branch modifies five files that already shipped (`ObservationChart.tsx`, `VitalsTable.tsx`, `vitals/list.tsx`, `observations.tsx`, `diagnostic-reports.tsx`, `DiagnosticReportView.tsx`, `DiagnosticReportResultsTable.tsx`). A regression in an existing clinical view is the worst outcome here — weigh it above anything in the new code.
3. **Whether any binding constraint above is violated anywhere in the branch.**
4. **Triage of the six deferred items.**
5. **Accessibility and clinical-safety issues** in the new UI. This is a table of patient values; a value associated with the wrong analyte or the wrong timestamp is the highest-severity class of bug in this diff.

Do not report style nits, missing tests already explained above, or suggestions to add features the spec deferred.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion. If the diff feels large for one pass, review it in passes yourself and say so.

## Output Format

Begin directly with the verdict. Every line is a verdict, a finding with file:line, or a check you ran.

### Merge Readiness
**[Ready to merge | Ready with caveats | Not ready]** — one sentence.

### Integration Findings
Cross-file bugs the per-task reviews could not have caught. file:line, what breaks, under what input. "None" if none.

### Regression Risk to Existing Surfaces
Per modified pre-existing file: what changed, and whether existing behaviour is preserved.

### Constraint Violations
Any binding constraint violated. "None" if none.

### Deferred-Item Triage
For each of the six: **Fix before merge** | **Fine to defer** — one line of reasoning each.

### Accessibility / Clinical Safety
Findings specific to correct value-to-analyte-to-timestamp association and assistive-tech usability.

All four are wired. Here's where to click.

**Start with the Plots tab — it's the one guaranteed to work.**

```
/facility/{facilityId}/patient/{patientId}/encounter/{encounterId}/plots
```

Click a plot card's **title** — "Blood Pressure", "Pulse", "Temperature". Blood Pressure is the best first test: it has two codes, so you'll get the Systolic/Diastolic pill row as well as the chart and table.

The other three:

| Where | What to click |
|---|---|
| Encounter → **Observations** tab | any observation card |
| Encounter → **Overview**, Vitals section | a **column header** (Pulse, Temperature…) |
| Diagnostic report view, or Encounter → **Diagnostic Reports** tab | the **analyte name** in the results table |

**The catch you'll hit immediately:** those three only become clickable when an observation has a `main_code`, and every question in the backend's fixture data lacks an observation code — `main_code` is copied straight from the question's `code`, so on a fixture database every observation has `main_code: null` and renders exactly as before, unclickable. That's deliberate, not a bug.

The Plots tab is exempt because its codes come from `public/config/plots.json`, not from questionnaires. It'll open even with zero readings — you'll get the empty state, and the scope toggle still works.

To make the other three light up, create a questionnaire with a numeric question bound to an observation code from the `system-observation` valueset — reuse one already in `plots.json`, e.g. Pulse (`8867-4`, `http://loinc.org`) — then submit it against the encounter two or three times with different values. Then you'll also get an actual line in the chart rather than just a table.

Inside the sheet: **This Enc. / + Prev** toggles between this encounter and the patient's whole history (each caches separately), the pills switch which code the chart plots, and scrolling the table right walks backwards in time and loads more.

input.prompt:
You are extending a completed, reviewed feature: the CARE "observation plot sheet" (React 19 + TypeScript EMR frontend). The user found a real gap during testing and it needs closing.

Work from: `/Users/bodhishthomas/code/care_fe/.claude/worktrees/observation-plot-sheet-77acfc`

## The gap

An observation can carry **components** — FHIR's `Observation.component` pattern, where one observation holds several related measurements. In this codebase:

```ts
interface ObservationComponent {
  value: QuestionnaireSubmitResultValue;  // { value?: string | null; unit?: Code; coding?: Code }
  interpretation?: Interpretation;
  reference_range?: ObservationReferenceRange[];
  code?: Code | null;
  note?: string;
}
```
(see `src/types/emr/observation/observation.ts`)

The feature currently ignores `component[]` entirely — verified, zero references. So a component-bearing observation renders as a single row keyed by `main_code` showing `observation.value.value`, which for a panel-style observation is typically empty, and its components are silently dropped. A "Complete Blood Count" observation carrying Hemoglobin / WBC / Platelets components shows one blank row instead of three populated ones.

The backend populates these in `create_components` (care repo, `care/emr/resources/questionnaire/utils.py`): each component gets `code` copied from the sub-question's code and its own `value`.

## The files (all in `src/components/Common/Charts/observation-plot-sheet/`)

Read all of these before changing anything — they are a reviewed, working system:
- `observationPivot.ts` — the pure core. `pivotObservations`, `seriesForCode`, `buildObservationQueryParams`, and the `PlotRow` / `PlotColumn` / `PlotPoint` types.
- `observationPivot.test.ts` — the project's ONLY unit test harness for this feature. 36 tests currently pass.
- `useObservationPlotData.ts` — the data hook; the feature's only API-aware module.
- `ObservationFlowsheetTable.tsx` — renders `columns` × `rows`.
- `ObservationPlotSheet.tsx` — the shell; owns active-code and scope state, renders the code pills.

## What to build

**1. Discover component codes from the data.** The caller passes `codes: Code[]`, but component codes cannot be known upfront — they must be discovered from the fetched observations. Rows become: the requested codes, plus every distinct component code found, in a stable order (requested codes first, then component codes in first-encountered order).

**2. A component shares its parent observation's `effective_datetime`**, so it belongs in the same column as its parent. No new column logic needed.

**3. Change what a cell holds.** `PlotColumn.cells` is currently `Record<string, ObservationListRead>`, which cannot represent a component. Introduce a resolved cell type carrying what the table actually needs — the value, its unit, the value type to format with, any note, and a reference back to the source observation. Something like:

```ts
export interface PlotCell {
  value?: string | null;
  unit?: string;
  valueType: QuestionType;
  note?: string;
  source: ObservationListRead;
}
```

Adapt the exact shape to what the table and chart genuinely need — do not add fields nothing reads. Note the table currently calls `formatValue(cell.value.value ?? undefined, cell.value_type)`; components have no `value_type` of their own, so decide what to format them with and say what you chose and why (the parent's `value_type` is one option; inspecting the component's own value shape is another).

**4. Suppress an empty main-code row.** If the main code has no value in ANY column — the typical panel case, where the parent observation is just a container — do not render a row of dashes for it. Keep it when it does carry values.

**5. `seriesForCode` must resolve component codes too**, so the chart plots a component series. Same numeric-only, oldest-first, one-point-per-timestamp rules that already apply.

**6. The pills in `ObservationPlotSheet` must come from the discovered rows**, not just the `codes` prop, so component codes are selectable. Keep the existing rule that the pill row is hidden when there is only one thing to pick.

## Constraints that still bind

- **No reference ranges, no normal/abnormal shading, no interpretation logic.** `ObservationComponent` carries `interpretation` and `reference_range` — ignore both. This was deliberately deferred because that data is usually absent.
- **Do not import `observationApi` anywhere except `useObservationPlotData`** — that invariant has been verified three times by reviewers.

- Preserve existing behaviour for observations WITHOUT components. This is additive; the four wired call sites and the existing tests must keep working.
- Preserve the existing first-wins duplicate rule (first reading at a given code+timestamp wins, because the API returns `-modified_date`).
- Preserve the timestamp guard: readings whose `effective_datetime` does not parse to a finite time are dropped. `date-fns format()` throws `RangeError` on `NaN`, which would crash the whole sheet.
- Code style: double quotes, 2-space indent, semicolons, `interface` for objects, **no `any`**, named exports. Beware inferred `any` from library type intersections — a green `tsc` has already missed one on this branch.
